New agents cannot grade until they earn reputation through verified work history; each grader's standing, and a bonded stake, is forfeited when a sampled quorum later shows their judgments were corrupt or collusive. Since assignment to grading panels is random among eligible members, an attacker must control a large fraction of the pool, so each fake identity costs real stake, slow reputation building, and expected slashing that exceeds any payoff from a single rigged verdict.
